userStories.title: Add pure chat effort helpers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the shared pure effort API used by chat model selection and the effort command.

**Motivation** — The `/model` picker lists ids exactly as configured (`tierModels` plus catalog discovery), so a model is offered only at the suffixes that happen to be configured, and changing effort means retyping the id.

**Approach** — **Effort helpers** (pure, new `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-effort.ts`). The levels a user can pick are `default` (no suffix — the provider's default) followed by nax-agent's `THINKING_LEVELS` in their declared order: `off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max`. `modelEffort(model)` reads the suffix with `parseModelSpec`; `withEffort(model, level)` rewrites it (`default` removes it); `cycleEffort(level, step)` moves one level left or right and wraps.

Read only: `parseModelSpec(raw): { model; effort? }` (`@nathapp/nax-agent`, `packages/nax-agent/src/cost/model-spec.ts`) — matches `<model>[<effort>]` where neither part contains a bracket. `THINKING_LEVELS: Record<ThinkingLevel, true>` (`@nathapp/nax-agent/internal`, `packages/nax-agent/src/native/models.ts`) — keys in order `off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max`.

New: `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-effort.ts` exporting `EFFORT_LEVELS`, `type EffortLevel`, `isEffortLevel(text)`, `modelEffort(model)`, `withEffort(model, level)`, `cycleEffort(level, step)`, re-exported from `packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts`.

A model id whose suffix is not a known level (`m[turbo]`): `modelEffort` returns `default`; `withEffort` replaces the unknown suffix. `isEffortLevel` itself matches exactly; command argument lowercasing belongs to US-004. Keep every slash of a model id when rewriting. Consume existing package exports, not deep source imports or a direct nax-ai import. Add the new helper tests at `packages/nax/test/unit/chat/chat-effort.test.ts`.

**Scope** — In: pure effort levels, parsing, rewriting, wrapping, and named chat barrel exports. Out: header/footer rendering (US-002), picker state/key handling (US-003), slash dispatch and the effort picker (US-004). Any change to `@nathapp/nax-agent`. Validating whether a given provider or model honours a thinking level; an unsupported level still reaches the provider, which `toThinkingLevel` already logs and ignores.

**Interface** — `EFFORT_LEVELS`, `type EffortLevel`, `isEffortLevel(text)`, `modelEffort(model)`, `withEffort(model, level)`, `cycleEffort(level, step)`; existing parser contract: `parseModelSpec(raw): { model; effort? }`; existing level registry: `THINKING_LEVELS: Record<ThinkingLevel, true>`.

[unit] modelEffort("opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash[high]") returns "high".

[unit] withEffort("opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash[high]", "default") returns "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash".
[unit] withEffort("m/x[turbo]", "high") returns "m/x[high]".
[unit] withEffort("huggingface/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7", "low") returns "huggingface/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7[low]", keeping every slash of the multi-slash id.

userStories.title: Keep effort visible in the chat header and footer
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve the full effort suffix in the real header/footer renderers and show the uncapped model name whenever the header has room.

**Motivation** — `shortModel` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts`) cuts any name longer than 24 characters to 23 plus `…`. Both the header (`headerTitleLine`) and the footer (`rightLine`) use it, so `deepseek-v4.1-flash[high]` (25 characters) shows as `deepseek-v4.1-flash[hig…` — the effort, the part that changes, is the part removed. The header has a whole row to spare.

**Approach** — **Display.** `shortModel` keeps a trailing `[effort]` suffix whole and elides only the name in front of it. The header's model segment drops the 24-character cap. When the first line does not fit, the product, version and mode stay fixed, the session title (from chat-resume-sessions) yields first, shrinking to nothing, and only then is the model's name elided, its suffix kept whole; with no room left for any of the name, the name collapses to the ellipsis alone and the suffix still follows it. A name with no suffix is elided at its end the same way. The header uses the theme's `glyphs.ellipsis` (`...` in the ASCII theme); `shortModel` keeps its literal `…`.

`shortModel` Target: the same text, but when it ends in `[<effort>]` the suffix is kept whole and only the part before it is cut, so the result is at most 24 characters plus the suffix length when the name alone exceeds 24, and is unchanged otherwise.

`headerTitleLine` Target: the text after the last `/` with no length cap, elided in its name part (suffix kept) only when the first line would exceed the header width.

`headerTitleLine` (`chat-status.ts`) — Baseline is the post-chat-resume-sessions `headerTitleLine(state, version, width, glyphs)` with its title span; the Target keeps that signature and applies the yield order above.

Use display-column measurement and the theme's actual ellipsis width; preserve existing single-row sanitization and suffix text, including unknown levels. Do not confuse the footer's 24-character name limit with a 24-character total suffix-inclusive limit. Modify `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts` and `packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/chat-status.test.ts`; add shortModel cases for a suffixed name and header cases for the uncapped model; the existing shortModel cases and the flatten case pass unchanged. Update the upstream test that intentionally expected an overflowing fixed model prefix because this feature now elides the model after the title yields. `packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/chat-status.test.ts` is 722 lines and `check:file-sizes` fails a test file over 800, so put the new header cases in a sibling file split by describe block (for example `packages/nax/test/unit/tui/chat/chat-status-header.test.ts`) rather than growing it past ~650 lines.

`shortModel`'s suffix rule (US-002) is reached from the footer and header renderers; US-002's ACs call `footerModel` and `headerLines`, the functions `ChatApp` draws from.

**Scope** — In: footer model shortening and header first-line width allocation, with session-title and sanitization regressions retained. Out: helper API implementation (US-001), effort selection and picker input/state (US-003), the effort command (US-004). Bounding the length of an `[effort]` suffix: `parseModelSpec` accepts any non-bracket text, and an unusually long configured suffix is drawn whole.

**Interface** — Preserve `headerTitleLine(state, version, width, glyphs)`; keep the existing `shortModel`, `footerModel`, and `headerLines` call interfaces.

userStories.title: Cycle model effort in the model picker
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let left/right arrows cycle the highlighted base model's pending effort and apply model and effort together on Return.

**Motivation** — The `/model` picker lists ids exactly as configured (`tierModels` plus catalog discovery), so a model is offered only at the suffixes that happen to be configured, and changing effort means retyping the id.

**Approach** — **`/model` picker.** Rows are de-duplicated by base model (the id without its suffix), in the order their first occurrence appears; a row's `value` is the base model, its `label` is `displayText(base)`, and the typed query filters on the base model (so typing `high` no longer matches a `[high]` suffix — intended). Each row remembers its original id (the current session model for the current row, else its first-seen id) and shows `effort <level>` in its detail column, where the level is that id's suffix text as written (`effort turbo` for an unknown suffix) or `default`. The pending efforts live in `useChatPicker`'s picker state, keyed by base model, and `choose` reads them synchronously the way it reads the pointer, so a → and a Return delivered in one input batch apply the cycled effort. ←/→ cycles the highlighted row's pending effort through `EFFORT_LEVELS` (an unknown suffix cycles as if it were `default`); Return switches to the row's original id when its effort was never cycled, else to `withEffort(base, pending)`.

`PickerEntry` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/Picker.tsx`) — the model picker's rows take `value` = base model and gain `original?: string` and `effortLabel?: string`; the detail column shows `effort <effortLabel>`.

`ownsPickerKey` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/Picker.tsx`) Target: `ownsPickerKey(key, kind)` — also left and right when `kind` is `model`.

`ChatPicker` (returned by `useChatPicker`) gains `cycle(entry: PickerEntry, step: 1 | -1): void`; `PickerProps` gains `onCycle?: (entry: PickerEntry, step: 1 | -1) => void`, which `Picker`'s key handler calls on ←/→ for a model row.

`PickerState` gains `pending: ReadonlyMap<string, EffortLevel>` (base model -> cycled level) for rendering; `useChatPicker` also keeps a ref mirror of that map, written by `cycle` and read by `choose`, so a `→` and a Return in one input batch — and repeated `→→` — read the latest level rather than the render's state. A cycle starts from the ref's level for that base, else from the row's effort label (`default` for an unknown suffix).

`PickerModelInput` gains `pending?: ReadonlyMap<string, EffortLevel>`; `pickerModel` sets a model row's `effortLabel` to the pending level when one exists, and sets `detail = "effort " + effortLabel`, so `entryRow` draws it like any other detail.

Wire `onCycle={picker.cycle}` at the existing `Picker` mount in `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx`. Preserve existing ref-backed query/pointer batching, model-only query editing, modified-key ownership, non-model pickers, and runControl error reporting. Initial pending maps are empty per opening; cancellation or choosing must not persist preferences. A rejected switch uses the existing transcript error route, just as `/model <id>` does.

Modify `packages/nax/test/ui/chat/picker.test.tsx` — model-picker rows now carry the base model as their value and a `effort <level>` detail; fixtures that list the same base model at two suffixes now expect one row, and assertions on a model row's full text gain the `effort <level>` detail. The existing file is at its hard line limit; keep tests and source within repository limits by factoring focused code/tests and reusing the harness where needed.

`withEffort` (US-001) is consumed by the `/model` picker (US-003) and `/effort` (US-004), and `cycleEffort` by the `/model` picker only; their ACs enter through the mounted `ChatApp` (typing `/model` or `/effort`) and assert the fake host's `switchTo` received the suffixed model id.

**Scope** — In: model-row de-duplication and display details, per-row pending efforts, synchronous cycle/choose state, model-only arrow handling, and ChatApp callback wiring. Out: display shortening (US-002), the new command and effort picker kind (US-004), changing shared model discovery, and reimplementing effort helpers (US-001). Persisting a per-model preferred effort across sessions; the session meta keeps the chosen model id with its suffix, as today. A notice in the transcript after a model or effort switch (feature chat-transcript-polish).

**Interface** — `original?: string`; `effortLabel?: string`; `ownsPickerKey(key, kind)`; `cycle(entry: PickerEntry, step: 1 | -1): void`; `onCycle?: (entry: PickerEntry, step: 1 | -1) => void`; `pending: ReadonlyMap<string, EffortLevel>`; `pending?: ReadonlyMap<string, EffortLevel>`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] pickerModel({ kind: "model", models: ["p/a[high]", "p/a[low]", "p/b"], currentModel: "p/b", currentMode: "guarded" }) returns two entries with values "p/a" and "p/b", in that order.
[unit] Given model choices ["p/a[high]", "p/a[low]", "p/b"] and currentModel "p/b", pickerModel returns the p/a entry with effortLabel "high", its first-seen suffix.
[unit] Given model choices ["p/a[high]", "p/a[low]", "p/b"] and currentModel "p/b", pickerModel returns the p/b entry with effortLabel "default".
[unit] Given model choices ["p/a[high]", "p/a[low]", "p/b"] and currentModel "p/a[low]", pickerModel returns the p/a entry with effortLabel "low".
[unit] Given model choices ["p/a[high]", "p/a[low]", "p/b"] and currentModel "p/a[low]", pickerModel returns the p/a entry with current: true.

[unit] Given pickerModel({ kind: "model", models: ["p/a[high]"], currentModel: "p/a[high]", currentMode: "guarded" }), pickerLayout renders its model row with the detail "effort high", corresponding to the row's effortLabel "high".
[unit] A model row first seen as m/x[turbo] shows the detail "effort turbo".
[integration] Return on an un-cycled m/x[turbo] row calls switchTo({ model: "m/x[turbo]" }), keeping the id as configured.
[integration] Given a highlighted p/a[high] row, when → and Return are delivered in one input batch, switchTo receives { model: "p/a[xhigh]" }, applying xhigh to that same base.
[integration] Typing the query high in the model picker keeps only rows whose base model contains high, not rows whose suffix is [high].

[integration] In a mounted ChatApp offering ["p/a[high]", "p/b"] with current model p/b, typing /model, then →, then Return on the first row calls the fake host's switchTo with { model: "p/a[xhigh]" }, matching { model: withEffort(<first row base>, cycleEffort(<its effort>, 1)) }.
[integration] Given a highlighted p/a[high] row, when ← then Return are pressed, switchTo receives { model: "p/a[medium]" }, applying the level one step lower.

[integration] Given rows p/a[high] then p/b[low] with the first row highlighted, when →, ↓, then Return are pressed, switchTo receives { model: "p/b[low]" } at the second row's own initial effort; the first row's change is not applied.
[integration] Given query high with p/high-model[high] highlighted, when ← or → is pressed, the highlighted row displays detail "effort medium" or "effort xhigh", respectively.
[integration] Given a model picker filtered by the typed query high, when ←/→ cycles the highlighted row's effort, the query remains high, leaving the query text unchanged.
[integration] When ←/→ is pressed in an open /resume picker, its rendered picker and transcript remain unchanged, including the picker's rows and highlighted entry.
[integration] ←/→ in the /resume picker does not call switchTo.
[integration] ←/→ in the /resume picker does not call resume.
[integration] A rejected switchTo from the model picker shows its error in the transcript, as /model <id> does.

When → and Return are used on an m/x[turbo] row, switchTo receives { model: "m/x[off]" }.
When a model row is cycled, the pointer moves away and returns, its detail still shows its own pending effort.

userStories.title: Add the effort command and level picker
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add /effort to change only the current model's reasoning effort, directly or through a level picker.

**Motivation** — The user asked for effort switching from the TUI (2026-10-28 ruling: picker ←/→ plus `/effort`).

**Approach** — **`/effort`.** A new built-in after `model` in `COMMANDS`. `/effort <level>` switches to `withEffort(current model, level)`; `/effort` with no argument opens a new `effort` picker whose rows are the eight levels with the current one marked `(current)`.

`PickerKind` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts`) Target: `"model" | "resume" | "mode" | "effort"`.

`TITLES` (`Picker.tsx`, `satisfies Record<PickerKind, string>`) gains `effort: "Reasoning effort"`.

`pickerModel` gains an `effort` branch: rows are `EFFORT_LEVELS` in order, the row equal to `modelEffort(currentModel)` marked current; the branch takes no query (like `mode`). The function's final branch no longer treats every other kind as `resume`.

`actionFor` gains an `effort` case: `host.switchTo({ model: withEffort(host.current().model, entry.value) })`, reading the host's model at choose time.

`COMMANDS` / `COMMAND_DESCRIPTIONS` — `"effort"` inserted right after `"model"`, described `"Switch reasoning effort"`.

Failure handling: `/effort <x>` with `x` not one of the eight levels: no switch; the command shows `unknown effort "<x>"; use one of: default, off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max`, echoing `x` as typed. The command lowercases its argument before calling `isEffortLevel`, which itself matches exactly. `/effort` with more than one argument: no switch; the command shows `usage: /effort [level]`. `/effort <level>` equal to the current effort: `switchTo` is called with the unchanged model and returns without reopening; nothing else happens. A model id whose suffix is not a known level (`m[turbo]`): `modelEffort` returns `default`; `withEffort` replaces the unknown suffix. `switchTo` rejects (provider unknown, open fails): the picker or command shows the error the same way `/model <id>` does today.

Modify slash dispatch and the existing picker, not ChatHost or provider validation. Both direct and picker selections go through the existing runControl/error route; no effort selection may call resume. Use the current model at the moment of choosing so a picker cannot apply its effort to a stale model id. The no-reopen case uses the host's existing exact model/mode equality check, not an early return based only on modelEffort; rewriting an unknown suffix still goes through withEffort and switchTo.

Modify `packages/nax/test/ui/chat/slash-menu.test.tsx` — the effort command now sits after the model command, shifting every later built-in down one row: the nine-down-arrow case that expected the plugins row now lands on the skills row (or takes one more press to reach plugins), and the beyond-the-window comment and the thirteen-matches title are updated to the new count. This checkout's registry has 14 commands before the addition, so use the actual resulting count of 15 rather than the stale test title's number.

Modify `packages/nax/test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx` — the help listing and the cases driven by the built-in command list now include the effort command and its description, between the model and sessions commands. Exercise mounted ChatApp for command dispatch, picker behavior, and slash-menu discovery; extend picker tests as needed without exceeding file-size limits.

**Scope** — In: effort built-in registration/help/menu, direct argument validation, the effort picker and its choose-time model rewrite, failure behavior, and affected menu regressions. Out: model-picker cycling (US-003), renderer width changes (US-002), helper implementation (US-001). A notice in the transcript after a model or effort switch (feature chat-transcript-polish). Changing effort for a subagent run (`agent.modelAliases`) or for `nax run`. Validating whether a given provider or model honours a thinking level; an unsupported level still reaches the provider, which `toThinkingLevel` already logs and ignores.

**Interface** — `PickerKind = "model" | "resume" | "mode" | "effort"`; `effort: "Reasoning effort"`; `host.switchTo({ model: withEffort(host.current().model, entry.value) })`; reuse `runSlashCommand`, `modelEffort`, `isEffortLevel`, and `withEffort` through existing module/barrel boundaries.

analysis:
Feature and prerequisite: This is an enhancement to the existing native chat UI, not a new chat or provider implementation. The chat-resume-sessions prerequisite is already represented in this checkout: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts:463 defines headerTitleLine(state, version, width, glyphs), and :469 constructs the optional session title. Preserve this signature and the title functionality while changing the width-allocation policy. All four stories implement code inside packages/nax; packages/nax-agent is read-only reference material. The binding execution order is US-001 first, US-002 and US-003 independently after it, then US-004 after US-001 and US-003. No additional stories or prerequisite implementation work are needed. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session; findings were obtained with direct file reads and text searches. No implementation changes or tests were run while drafting this PRD.

Existing effort boundary: packages/nax-agent/src/cost/model-spec.ts:29 defines the anchored suffix grammar, and :31 exposes parseModelSpec(raw). Only well-formed trailing bracket pairs with non-bracket, nonempty components are stripped; malformed strings remain opaque model ids. packages/nax-agent/src/index.ts:78 publicly exports parseModelSpec. packages/nax-agent/src/native/models.ts:41 parses the suffix before splitting on the FIRST slash, preserving multi-slash model ids; :71 defines THINKING_LEVELS in the required off/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max order; :100 translates unknown levels to the provider default with a warning.
